clue.text: Most awful table thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters of the two words before it are tossed around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Most of a dreadful piece of furniture has been discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' looks like an intensifier for 'awful', but it is the definition; 'thrown out' rearranges AWFUL TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying nearly every one of a group is a synonym for the majority, so the phrase can replace 'most'.

clue.text: On strike exclusively in this area?

definitions.text: On strike exclusively in this area?

parts.words: On strike exclusively in this area?
parts.note: in cricket the on side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs, so a batsman scoring only there strikes only on one side

explanation.surface: A question about where a workforce is staging a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On strike' suggests industrial action; in cricket 'on' is the name for one half of the field, and the batsman on strike is the one facing the bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the on side and the leg side are two names for the same half of the field.

clue.text: Bread roll container Ethel found empty

parts.note: a bag is a simple container

indicators.note: found empty means the name Ethel loses its middle, keeping just its outside letters

explanation.surface: Ethel discovers that the box for the rolls has nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled and then baked.

clue.text: Brewed beers out with some certitude in Dublin

indicators.note: brewed suggests ingredients being mixed and fermented, so the letters that follow are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Beer having been brewed, it is served with confidence in the Irish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' rearranges BEERS and OUT together; the definition is a stage-Irish phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is the stock Irish expression of assurance, meaning certainly or of course.

clue.text: Time I'm shut in for done in Maze

indicators.note: a maze is a tangle of passages, so placing these words in a maze jumbles their letters

explanation.surface: Someone says they are locked inside, exhausted, in a maze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maze' is the anagram signal, and the 'in' just before it is only a link word; the definition is the single word at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists treat time as a further dimension added to the three of space.

clue.text: Marsupial finds love with doctor in temple

indicators.note: in tells us the love and doctor pieces are placed inside the temple word

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
love is nil in tennis, written as O
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: An Australian animal finds romance with a physician inside a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing Australian marsupial that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Exaggerated sales promotion essential to pushy people

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Overblown marketing is something aggressive people cannot do without.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is inflated publicity used to push a product, a direct synonym for over-the-top promotion.

clue.text: Difficult to attempt to win where Agassi rarely lost

parts.note: difficult means hard
to court someone is to try to win their affection

explanation.surface: It is tough to try to beat a tennis champion on his best playing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi, the American tennis player, won most of his titles on this concrete or acrylic surface.

clue.text: Succeed? Anything but where pennies decline in value

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pence or pennies
prices that recede fall back or diminish

explanation.surface: A question whether one can prosper where small coins are losing their worth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an opposite: one meaning of 'succeed' is to come after, and this word means to come before.
explanation.definitionFit: To go before is the reverse of to follow on after, which is one sense of the clue's first word.

clue.text: One giant highly impatient

parts.note: one can be the indefinite article a
Gog is one of the legendary giants Gog and Magog, guardians of the City of London

explanation.surface: A huge being is extremely restless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eagerly expectant and unable to wait is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Great outcry bringing down crows

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue
a murder is the collective noun for a flock of crows

explanation.surface: Loud protests that make the birds fall from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is not a direction but low spirits; 'crows' is not a verb but the birds' collective noun. The idiom is to scream this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom to scream this, it means a loud and furious protest.

clue.text: Scene initially seen in W.C.

parts.note: a field is a scene or sphere of activity

indicators.note: initially says we take just the opening letter of the word seen

explanation.surface: A sight first glimpsed in the lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: W.C. looks like a toilet, but it is the initials of the American comic actor whose surname is the answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: W.C. Fields was the American film comedian, so his initials point to his surname.

clue.text: Traditional roofer is a man of straw

definitions.meaning: a craftsman who covers roofs with reed or straw in the old way
literally someone whose working material is straw, playing on the idiom for a weak person

explanation.definitionFit: Thatching uses straw or reed, so the old-style roofer literally works with straw.

clue.text: On about last ball formally delivered

indicators.note: on about says the ball word sits around the outside of the other word

parts.note: red is a ball in snooker
an ender is the thing that comes last

explanation.surface: Something about the final delivery of a cricket over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last ball' looks like the final delivery of an over, but the two words do separate jobs, and 'On about' is the container signal; in snooker the red is a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict or account is rendered when it is officially handed over or given.

clue.text: Maybe bullish competitors started fighting before noon

indicators.note: fighting suggests a scrap, so the letters of started tumble into a new order

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: Aggressive rivals began a brawl in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bullish' suggests aggression; it really refers to aiming at the bull, the centre of a dartboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A team of players who throw at a board and aim for the bull fits 'bullish competitors'.

clue.text: Employer's admission to serious error

indicators.note: admission to says the answer is let in among the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A boss confesses to a grave mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admission' suggests confession, but it signals letters admitted inside SERIOUS ERROR; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses or employs something is a user, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Presumably no sandwiches short of a picnic?

definitions.text: Presumably no sandwiches short of a picnic?

parts.words: Presumably no sandwiches short of a picnic?
parts.note: plays on the phrase 'a sandwich short of a picnic', meaning not very bright; a full picnic suggests full mental faculties

explanation.surface: A question about whether a picnic has its full quota of sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone mentally sharp, the opposite of being a sandwich short of a picnic.

clue.text: Jelly in silver works shortly

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: shortly says the word for works is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: artworks are art

explanation.surface: A gel made in a silversmith's workshop soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like 'soon' but tells us to cut the last letter from ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly made from seaweed, used in cooking and for growing microbes.

clue.text: Energy source clues go badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of clues go are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Puzzle hints are a poor source of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is the sugar cells burn for energy, so it is a source of energy.

clue.text: An ass of a driver? On the contrary!

definitions.text: An ass of a driver? On the contrary!

parts.words: An ass of a driver? On the contrary!
parts.note: looks like an insult to a bad motorist; reversed, it is a driver of an ass-like animal

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a foolish motorist, swiftly reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A muleteer drives mules, close relatives of the ass, so he is a driver of asses.

clue.text: Joy beheaded family member

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the family word is removed

parts.note: a relation is a member of one's family

explanation.surface: Delight at a relative's execution.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness, a direct synonym of joy.

clue.text: Maverick Mike is in fine fettle

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
someone in fine fettle is fit and healthy

explanation.surface: Mike, the independent sort, is in excellent health.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit is someone who does not conform, like a maverick.

clue.text: What's to be, or not to be rewritten in quotes?

definitions.text: What's to be, or not to be

indicators.note: rewritten says the letters of in quotes are written out again in a different order

explanation.surface: Asks whether Hamlet's famous line has been misquoted.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's line ends 'that is the question', so the definition is the thing the speech names.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hamlet, 'to be, or not to be' is called the question, so it defines the noun.

clue.text: Hotel denied Asian utensil for frying snake

indicators.note: denied says the hotel letter is refused, removed from the Asian word

parts.note: a Thai is a person from Thailand, an Asian
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pan is used for frying

explanation.surface: A hotel refuses an Asian guest a pan to fry a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The taipan is a highly venomous Australian snake.

clue.text: Some panic in going for sweet addition

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little alarm on leaving, for something sweet added.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with its 'for': the answer is what one adds for sweetness.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is a sugary coating added to cakes to sweeten them.

clue.text: In and out I see Hodge at last in government department

parts.note: being in means being at home
a light that is out is off
see is pronounced like the letter C

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the name Hodge

explanation.surface: Someone notes Hodge going in and out of a ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Hodge is a British politician, which helps the government picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Office is the UK ministry for policing, immigration and security.

clue.text: Double firsts not quite attained in academic stream

indicators.note: not quite means each copy loses its final letter
double says the first word is written out twice

parts.note: 1st is written as IST in crosswords

explanation.surface: Two top degrees almost achieved at university.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name of the River Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the stretch of the Thames at Oxford, so a university river.

clue.text: Resistance encountered in stone structure that develops

indicators.note: encountered in says the resistance letter is found inside the stone word

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Opposition met inside a building made of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stone structure' looks like one phrase, but the definition starts at 'structure'.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is the rudimentary part of an organism from which it grows.

clue.text: Thomas perhaps taken out by gangland principal in 9

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of taken are knocked out of order
in tells us the gangland letter goes inside the number word

parts.note: 9 is the number nine written as a word

indicators.note: principal means first, so we take the opening letter of gangland

explanation.surface: Thomas killed by the head of a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a cross-reference to 9 across but is just the number written as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas the Tank Engine is the children's railway character, so he is an example.
